strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing the practical challenge of balancing set size and class-conditional coverage in long-tailed classification
Rigorous theoretical analysis using Neyman-Pearson lemma to characterize oracle optimal sets for macro-coverage (Proposition 1)

Comprehensive experimental evaluation with two large-scale datasets (1,081 and 8,142 classes), multiple evaluation metrics, and careful methodology including truncated datasets for reliable rare-class evaluation
Three complementary methods offering different trade-offs between simplicity and theoretical guarantees (PAS, FUZZY CP, INTERP-Q)
Thoughtful design for practical deployment including handling classes with few/zero calibration examples and meaningful human decision-maker study (Section 3.2)
Detailed case study demonstrating impact on endangered species identification in Pl@ntNet
Reproducibility: code availability, extensive appendices with experimental details and additional ablations
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: PAS is straightforward application of framework to new score function; FUZZY CP applies existing weighted conformal prediction techniques; INTERP-Q lacks theoretical guarantees
Macro-coverage assumption is problematic for stated motivation of prioritizing rare classes; extension to weighted macro-coverage (Appendix D) should be in main narrative
Class mapping for FUZZY CP (Π_prevalence) is heuristic; counterintuitively underperforms more principled quantile-based mapping without clear explanation
Reconformalization step for FUZZY CP requires splitting calibration data into two subsets, reducing effective training samples; computational cost implications underexplored
Finite-sample analysis is missing: Proposition 1 is population-level with no bounds on approximation error from p̂(y|x) and p̂(y) estimation; INTERP-Q lacks any coverage guarantee

Experimental methodology concerns: validation set reused for both model selection and conformal calibration violates exchangeability assumption (impact not quantified); truncated datasets removing <101-example classes weaken evaluation of core motivation
Hyperparameter tuning (σ for FUZZY, τ for INTERP-Q) requires calibration-set selection without principled cross-validation procedure; robustness not thoroughly explored
Incomplete practical guidance: when should practitioners choose macro-coverage (Approach I) vs. class-conditional coverage (Approach II)? No clear decision criteria provided
Limited analysis of edge cases: behavior when p̂(y) is very small (numerical instability), sensitivity to classifier calibration quality, robustness to label shift between calibration and test

strengths: Well-motivated problem on long-tailed classification with practical importance (plant identification)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation on large-scale datasets (1K-8K classes) with multiple metrics and ablations
Theoretical grounding via Neyman-Pearson lemma for deriving optimal score function
Multiple complementary approaches offering practitioners design flexibility
Clear writing and well-organized presentation
weaknesses: Limited novelty: applies existing weighted conformal prediction and classical statistical results to a new setting; main contribution is incremental
Macro-coverage objective poorly motivated: contradicts stated goal of high class-conditional coverage for all classes; allows some classes to have arbitrarily poor coverage
Experimental setup concerns: truncated datasets weaken long-tail claims; validation set reuse violates exchangeability assumptions; noisy coverage estimates for rare classes
FUZZY CP requires extensive tuning (class mapping Π, bandwidth σ) with unclear sensitivity; alternative mappings fail without clear explanation
Modest empirical improvements: macro-coverage gains are incremental (~0.8-0.9 vs ~0.8-0.85); decision accuracy improvements are marginal
Limited baselines: only conformal methods compared; missing non-conformal uncertainty quantification approaches
Practical concerns: reconformalization requires 5K holdout examples; unclear how methods scale to other long-tail domains beyond plant identification

strengths: Well-motivated problem with strong practical relevance grounded in real applications (plant/animal identification, endangered species monitoring)
Novel theoretical contribution: macro-coverage objective is well-justified via Neyman-Pearson lemma, providing principled motivation for PAS score function
Multiple complementary approaches offering flexibility: parameter-free PAS for macro-coverage or tunable FUZZY CP for stronger class-conditional guarantees
Comprehensive evaluation: multiple metrics, realistic long-tailed datasets, novel simulated human decision-maker experiments, concrete case studies, thorough appendix analyses
Methods are practical and implementable with promised code release; detailed experimental protocol supports reproducibility
Clear articulation of trade-offs and limitations; honest discussion of when each method applies
weaknesses: FUZZY CP builds incrementally on existing weighted conformal prediction (Podkopaev & Ramdas 2021, Barber et al. 2023); novelty over prior work could be articulated more sharply
Class mapping Π_prevalence lacks strong theoretical justification; practical guidance for new domains is limited and primarily empirical
Limited scope: evaluated only on vision datasets with softmax scores; unclear generalization to other domains or score functions
Macro-coverage intentionally permits some classes to have poor coverage; implications for rare classes (central to long-tailed settings) deserve deeper analysis
Data splitting for FUZZY CP reconformalization (5000 examples) infeasible for smaller datasets; double use of validation set violates exchangeability in theory despite empirical justification
Truncated datasets (classes with <101 examples removed) and 100 test examples per class somewhat contradict 'truly long-tailed' claim; no comparison to non-conformal long-tailed methods
Figure 4 difficult to parse; limited sensitivity analysis to classifier quality and hyperparameter choices; missing ablation studies

strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing a real practical challenge in long-tailed classification with clear real-world applications (plant identification, biodiversity monitoring)
Solid theoretical justification for PAS score via Neyman-Pearson lemma, with extension to weighted macro-coverage
Comprehensive experimental evaluation on large-scale realistic datasets (1,081 and 8,142 classes) with multiple complementary metrics and careful experimental design
Multiple complementary approaches (PAS, WPAS, INTERP-Q) offering flexibility for different use cases
Practical value demonstrated through case studies (endangered species) and clear improvements over baselines with minimal computational overhead
Good reproducibility practices including detailed experimental procedures, proper data splitting for exchangeability, and mentioned code availability
Simulation of human decision-maker behavior (Section 3.3) provides practical perspective beyond standard metrics
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: PAS is a straightforward score function once the target (p(y|x)/p(y)) is identified; INTERP-Q is simple linear interpolation between existing methods' thresholds

Theoretical contributions are largely incremental applications of the Neyman-Pearson lemma rather than novel theoretical developments; no finite-sample analysis of approximation quality with estimated p̂(y|x) and p̂(y)
INTERP-Q's 1-2α coverage guarantee is substantially weaker than 1-α claimed guarantee with limited analysis of conservatism
Narrow evaluation scope: only computer vision datasets, only 2 datasets, only ResNet-50 architecture, no comparison with non-conformal long-tail learning methods
Macro-coverage may not be the right target for practitioners; paper doesn't deeply explore when macro-coverage vs class-conditional coverage is appropriate or provide clear guidance
FUZZY method's complexity (Π mapping, kernel selection, bandwidth tuning, reconformalization) is not justified by performance improvements; acknowledged to not outperform simpler INTERP-Q
Parameter selection lacks principled guidance (τ for INTERP-Q chosen via calibration set despite violating exchangeability; σ for FUZZY requires gridsearch)
No statistical significance testing or confidence intervals; results appear to be single runs without error quantification, particularly problematic for rare classes with limited test examples
Missing ablations on impact of using estimated vs. true class prevalence for PAS; nonlinear relationship between τ and set size in INTERP-Q is noted but not explained
Human evaluation uses synthetic decision-makers rather than actual human studies; mentioned 'effort' concept is not incorporated into the framework

strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing practical long-tail classification with clear real-world applications (plant identification, biodiversity monitoring)
Solid theoretical foundation using Neyman-Pearson lemma to characterize oracle-optimal sets for macro-coverage
Comprehensive experimental evaluation on two large-scale datasets (1,081 and 8,142 classes) with multiple complementary metrics
Multiple solution approaches (PAS, WPAS, INTERP-Q, FUZZY) acknowledging different trade-offs and application requirements
Practical case studies including endangered species protection and simulated human decision-makers
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: PAS is a straightforward application of conformal prediction with a new score function; INTERP-Q is simple linear interpolation of quantiles

Critical theory-practice gap: Proposition 1 assumes oracle knowledge of p(y|x) and p(y), but no error analysis provided for estimated densities p̂(y|x) and p̂(y); approximation quality never formalized
Weak coverage guarantee for INTERP-Q: only achieves 1-2α marginal coverage (Proposition 3), not the claimed 1-α; bound is not verified empirically

Macro-coverage is under-justified as primary target metric; macro-coverage treats all classes equally, but many applications (disease diagnosis, endangered species) need non-uniform coverage; WPAS adds hyperparameter selection burden

Significant hyperparameter selection issues: INTERP-Q requires choosing τ but suggested calibration approach violates exchangeability; FUZZY CP requires specifying class mapping Π and bandwidth σ with unclear guidance

Incomplete experimental comparisons: dismisses APS baseline without direct comparison; limited recent baseline methods; truncated dataset results show diminished differences, raising questions about problem scope

Theory-to-practice approximation never quantified: PAS is said to 'approximately' optimize macro-coverage but convergence rates, approximation bounds, or sensitivity to density estimation errors are not provided
FUZZY CP complexity not adequately discussed in main paper: Appendix D.2 shows significant sensitivity to Π choice (prevalence-based works best) but no principled selection method provided

strengths: Addresses an important and understudied problem: balancing class-conditional coverage with set size in long-tailed classification under conformal prediction
Principled theoretical derivation using Neyman-Pearson lemma showing optimal thresholding on prevalence-adjusted scores

Comprehensive experimental evaluation on genuinely large-scale datasets (1,081 and 8,142 classes) with multiple evaluation metrics and thoughtful extensions (endangered species, human decision-makers, focal loss comparison)
Practical methods that are simple to implement and provide clear guidance on when to use each approach
Excellent presentation, clear motivation with compelling plant identification application, and strong reproducibility standards
Addresses real practical applications relevant to biodiversity monitoring and citizen science platforms
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: PAS is straightforward prevalence weighting; INTERP-Q is simple linear interpolation; theoretical results are relatively direct applications of existing lemmas
Macro-coverage is a significant relaxation of the stated goal of high class-conditional coverage for all classes—some rare classes can have poor coverage if common classes compensate
Loose theoretical guarantees for INTERP-Q: the 1−2α marginal coverage bound is acknowledged as conservative with no empirical validation of actual tightness
Parameter selection lacks principled guidance: τ selection for INTERP-Q violates exchangeability by design; FUZZY requires choosing mapping Π and bandwidth σ with limited guidance
PAS depends on accurate estimates of p(y|x) and p(y) which are challenging for rare classes; missing sensitivity analysis to estimation errors
FUZZY method adds significant complexity but doesn't consistently outperform simpler INTERP-Q, suggesting added complexity is not justified
Evaluation limited to fine-grained image classification; transferability to other domains unclear with only two datasets tested
Human evaluation is simulated rather than using real humans; synthetic expert model is unrealistic
Missing analysis: computational complexity, scaling beyond 8,142 classes, coverage degradation for rarest classes, sensitivity to classifier quality
